newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sweet crudes perk up as May/June slips late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sweet crudes perk up as May/June slips late.

text.p: U.S. sweet cash grades perked up in late U.S. trading on Thursday, reflecting the weakening May/June spread for West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, traders said.
May WTI was trading around $19.80-90 a barrel Thursday afternoon, up 20 cents from late Wednesday, traders said.
June WTI was pegged around $20.00-10 a barrel.
The May/June roll was assessed around minus 25-15 cents a barrel, down from plus 30 cents early today.
May activity was winding down ahead of pipeline scheduling day on Friday.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James last traded at WTI plus 20 cents a barrel, compared to minus 10 at flat in the early afternoon.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was pegged at minus 50-30 cents a barrel, up 30 cents from earlier in the day.
WTI/Midland was even at minus 41-36 cents.
Sour Crudes were steady at weak ranges. West Texas Sour/Midland was assessed at WTI minus $1.75-60 a barrel, with minus $1.70 last done.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus was at $1.55-70 a barrel, with the highest trade at $2.10 and the lowest at $1.80, traders said.

The outright price rise was attributed to a report that U.S. oil inspectors were detained by a Kurdish group in Iraq, raising concerns about the sustainability of the oil-for-food deal on the eve of its renewal.
